public_rationale: Marcus says OpenAI's quarterly losses quadrupled right before its IPO. The WSJ report he cites, as relayed by several outlets, says the operating loss rose from $9.3 billion in Q1 2026 to $12.3 billion in Q2. That is a 32% rise, about 1.3 times, not four times. The Q1 figure is confirmed separately by The Information. His own quoted tweet says losses grew by $3 billion. Losses did widen, but they did not quadruple.
limitations: Figures come from press reports of investor documents, not audited filings.
A year-over-year comparison could not be checked, but the context is quarter over quarter.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI's quarterly losses quadrupled right before its IPO, which is undesirable.

statement.excerpt: You don’t want your quarterly losses to quadruple right before your IPO.

from_speaker: refers to the WSJ report that losses grew by $3 billion from Q1 to Q2 2026, to $12.3 billion
our_interpretation: Plain reading: OpenAI's quarterly loss in Q2 2026 was about four times its Q1 2026 loss.
The context cites the WSJ's Q1-to-Q2 comparison, so the comparison is quarter over quarter. The loss measure is the operating loss the WSJ reported.
'Quadruple' means a ratio near 4x; anything far below, such as about 1.3x, contradicts it.
criteria.support_condition: Reported figures showing OpenAI's Q2 2026 loss was roughly four times its Q1 2026 loss.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reported figures showing Q2 2026 loss was far less than four times the Q1 2026 loss.
